# OIOS by Omnia Intelligence AI

> OIOS installs AI Operating Systems for small businesses. Ours is named Jarvis. He briefs the
> owner by 7 AM, keeps the schedule, drafts the follow-ups and the past-due invoice chases, and
> reads back anything that can't be undone before it fires. Month 1 is the install plus the first
> build live by Day 7. Month-to-month, and the owner owns every tool, integration and note.

## Core Pages
- [What Jarvis does](https://getoios.com/features): The eight things owners hand him in the first month, each tagged "does it", "does it quietly" or "asks first"
- [How a request moves](https://getoios.com/how-it-works): Say it, he works, the read-back, your yes, the receipt — plus the guardrails underneath
- [Thirteen things you can say to Jarvis](https://getoios.com/solutions): Real sentences owners say and what happens when they do
- [Month 1](https://getoios.com/pricing): What the first thirty days include and what the engagement is scoped against
- [Why we built Jarvis](https://getoios.com/about): Wes Overstreet ran a landscape lighting company for ten years across seven cities and needed a COO he couldn't afford

## What Jarvis actually does
- A briefing at 7 AM: what happened overnight, what's on today, what needs the owner
- Keeps the schedule, writes the confirmations and reminders
- Drafts quotes, follow-ups and review requests against the business's real prices
- Drafts a chase for anyone 30 days past due and files it in the owner's drafts — he never sends it himself
- Remembers what he's told, in plain text files the owner owns and can take with them
- Files notes and runs a nightly sweep that flags what drifted and fixes nothing on its own
- Reads the sites and tools the business already uses, fills forms, builds carts — and stops at the money
- Builds software: a branch and a working preview, live once the owner approves it

## The guardrail
Anything irreversible — sending money, paying a bill, cancelling a job, deleting a record, placing
an order — stops and is read back to the owner first: the item, the total, the destination, and the
card by its last four only. That floor is enforced in code at the tool-call boundary, not by a
prompt, and no setting lowers it. Full card numbers are never spoken or logged. "Turn off autonomy"
switches off everything Jarvis does on his own; anything he did unasked reverses in one step.

## What OIOS does not claim
- Jarvis does not answer inbound customer phone calls. Phone answering is a separate OIOS install.
- The schedule is Jarvis's own, not a sync with an external calendar.
- Accounting data is read-only: he drafts invoice chases, the owner sends them.
- Background builds stop at a branch or a pull request. A human merges.
- There is no self-serve signup and no published pricing. Every engagement is scoped and quoted.
